title: HIRES favors the early DRS 28-day template over SERVAL in 16 fixed GJ 667C noise tests
abstract: We compare two early HARPS mean templates for the known 28-day GJ 667C signal with 45 independent-instrument HIRES exposures. Both templates have a free amplitude and the same nuisance terms. DRS has lower fitted loss in all 16 cases: two photon cuts, two nuisance models and four fixed white or correlated noise models. Residual-scaled Gaussian simulations at the fitted SERVAL mean give score tails from 0.0023 to 0.0236. A broader amplitude scan raises the maximum tails to 0.0058 to 0.0401. Thus the preference survives free scaling in these specified models, but its strength depends on noise and sample choices. The cases reuse observations and are not independent replications. We do not propagate the full early orbit uncertainty or infer a physical stellar-noise model. The result compares mean templates; it does not establish a new planet or a general extraction advantage. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and external-data retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: DRS has lower loss in each main nuisance-model case. Simulation ranges show how fitted truths and residual-scaled noise affect the score. Positive scores favor DRS. The ranges are conditional simulation intervals, not confidence intervals for the physical orbit.
